summary: 孙休崩后迎立，初有善政，旋以暴虐著称：杀张尚、任何定、改元无度；天纪四年晋六路伐吴，面缚出降，吴亡，封归命侯。
summary_en: Installed after Sun Xiu's death, he governed well at first, then grew notorious for cruelty: slaying Zhang Shang, favoring He Ding, changing eras without count; in the 4th year of Tianji, with Jin invading on six roads, he surrendered bound and bare, ending Wu, and was enfeoffed Marquis of Guiming.

portrait.appearance_basis: 史载「皓之为人，心性凶悖」。画像宜表现骄盈暴戾的末代君主之态，衣冠从孙吴末制。属艺术想象。

timeline.title: 生
timeline.summary: 孙权孙，太子和之子，封乌程侯。
timeline.summary_en: Grandson of Sun Quan, son of the crown prince He, enfeoffed Marquis of Wucheng.

timeline.title: 即位
timeline.summary: 孙休崩，群臣迎立乌程侯皓，改元元兴；初有令誉，旋露凶暴。
timeline.summary_en: On Sun Xiu's death the court brought in the Marquis of Wucheng; after a good start his savagery showed itself.

timeline.title: 诛濮阳兴张布
timeline.title_en: Puru Yangxing and Zhang Bu Slain
timeline.summary: 迎立功臣濮阳兴、张布以谏被诛，凶虐之端自此。
timeline.summary_en: The ministers who brought him in, Puru Yangxing and Zhang Bu, were slain for remonstrance — the first marks of his tyranny.

timeline.title: 迁都武昌旋还
timeline.title_en: The Capital Moved to Wuchang and Back
timeline.summary: 迁都武昌，民怨「宁饮建业水，不食武昌鱼」，寻还建业。
timeline.summary_en: He moved the capital to Wuchang; the people grumbled "rather drink Jianye's water than eat Wuchang's fish," and he soon returned.

timeline.title: 陆抗守西陵
timeline.summary: 步阐降晋，陆抗率军收复西陵，晋援不克。
timeline.summary_en: Bu Chan defected to Jin; Lu Kang retook Xiling, and the Jin relief failed.

timeline.title: 何定弄权
timeline.summary: 佞臣何定用事，典兵擅权，众皆侧目。
timeline.summary_en: The flatterer He Ding came to power, commanded troops, and overreached, drawing every eye against him.

timeline.title: 杀张尚等
timeline.summary: 侍中张尚以言语忤旨被诛，谏诤之路遂绝。
timeline.summary_en: The attendant Zhang Shang was put to death for words that offended, and the road of remonstrance closed.

timeline.title: 改元频繁
timeline.summary: 数年间频改元以应符瑞，朝纲愈乱。
timeline.summary_en: Year after year he changed the era to match portents, and the government fell further into disorder.

timeline.title: 晋六路伐吴
timeline.summary: 晋武帝命王濬、杜预等六路伐吴，建业震动。
timeline.summary_en: Emperor Wu of Jin sent Wang Jun, Du Yu, and others against Wu on six roads, shaking Jianye itself.

timeline.title: 孙皓降
timeline.summary: 皓面缚舆榇，出降于王濬军前，吴亡，封归命侯。
timeline.summary_en: Bound bare with the coffin at his cart, Hao surrendered before Wang Jun's army; Wu perished, and he was made Marquis of Guiming.

timeline.title: 薨于洛阳
timeline.summary: 举家迁洛阳，年四十二卒于洛阳。
timeline.summary_en: Brought with his house to Luoyang, he died there at forty-two.

timeline.title: 粗暴骄盈
timeline.summary: 史评称皓凶顽骄暴，虐杀朝臣，亲昵小人，吴之亡实由其自取。
timeline.summary_en: The histories call Hao brutal and arrogant, slaying his courtiers, clinging to petty men — Wu's ruin self-inflicted.

bio_md:
# 吴末帝 · 主要事迹

孙皓字元宗，孙权孙，废太子孙和之子，封乌程侯。永安六年孙休崩，丞相濮阳兴、左将军张布以太子年幼，迎立皓，改元元兴。皓初立，发优诏、恤士民、开仓廪，虚誉满朝野；然未及数月，凶暴之性毕露——元兴元年，即诛迎立功臣濮阳兴、张布，自此「滥杀之端」大开。

皓之暴政，史不绝书：性嗜酒，强臣下灌醉以伺其过；好杀人，剥面凿眼，酷刑备至；宠佞臣何定，杀侍中张尚，谏诤之路遂绝。甘露元年迁都武昌，民怨沸腾，谣曰「宁饮建业水，不食武昌鱼；宁还建业死，不止武昌居」，寻还建业。数年间频改元以应符瑞，天册、天玺之号纷至，朝纲日乱。

天纪四年，晋武帝六路伐吴，王濬楼船下益州，杜预、王浑等并进；陆抗已前卒，吴无良将。三月，王濬兵临建业，皓面缚舆榇，出降于军门——吴自孙权称帝至此凡五十二年而亡，三分归晋，天下复统。

皓举家迁洛阳，晋封归命侯，太康四年薨，年四十二。史家评曰：皓「凶顽骄暴，虐杀无度」，吴之亡非亡于晋之强，而亡于皓之暴——「既失民心，又失天命」，亡国之君，无有甚于皓者。然观其初立之善政，可见其非无才者，暴虐之性一朝得志，遂不可制，可为专制之戒。

> 参考：点校本《三国志》卷048《三嗣主传》、卷058《陆抗传》及晋书卷003《武帝纪》。

bio_parts_en.value:
Sun Hao, styled Yuanzong, was a grandson of Sun Quan, son of the deposed crown prince He, enfeoffed Marquis of Wucheng. In the 6th year of Yong'an, after Sun Xiu's death, the chancellor Puru Yangxing and General Zhang Bu, deeming the child heir too weak, installed Hao, changing the era to Yuanxing. At first he issued kind decrees, relieved the people, and opened the granaries, winning a fine reputation throughout the court; within months his savagery showed itself — in the 1st year of Yuanxing he slew Puru Yangxing and Zhang Bu, the very men who had enthroned him, and the age of reckless killing opened.

His tyranny fills the histories: a lover of wine who forced his ministers drunk to catch their slips; a killer who used flaying and eye-gouging among his torments; he favored the flatterer He Ding, slew the attendant Zhang Shang, and closed the road of remonstrance. In the 1st year of Ganlu he moved the capital to Wuchang until the people's cry — "rather drink Jianye's water than eat Wuchang's fish; rather die back in Jianye than dwell in Wuchang" — forced his return. Era followed era to match portents — Tiance, Tianxi — and the government fell into chaos.

In the 4th year of Tianji Emperor Wu of Jin invaded on six roads: Wang Jun's fleet came down from Yizhou, Du Yu and Wang Hun pressed from every side; Lu Kang was dead, and Wu had no great general left. In the third month Wang Jun reached Jianye, and Hao, bound bare with the coffin in his cart, surrendered at the army gate — Wu, fifty-two years from Sun Quan's imperial title, was no more, and the realm was reunified under Jin.

Brought with his house to Luoyang, he was made Marquis of Guiming by Jin, and died there in the 4th year of Taikang at forty-two. The historians' verdict: "brutal, stubborn, arrogant, cruel beyond measure" — Wu fell not to the strength of Jin but to his own tyranny: "he had lost the people's hearts and Heaven's mandate alike." No fallen sovereign surpasses him in infamy. Yet his opening reforms show a man of some ability; the tyrant in him, once loosed, could not be checked — a lesson for unchecked power.

> References: the punctuated critical edition of the *Sanguozhi*, ch. 48 ("Biographies of the Three Successors"), ch. 58 (biography of Lu Kang), and the *Jinshu*, ch. 3 ("Benji of Emperor Wu").
